objectives.text: Answer 'choose TWO' questions by tracking each option as it is mentioned, rejected or confirmed.
Follow a spoken process in order and complete a flow chart within the word limit.
Distinguish the current method from earlier or rejected methods and numbers.

levels.foundation: Answer-type predictions checked before listening; a teacher-controlled second play with pauses after each stage, recorded as support.
levels.core: Answer all ten questions after one play, with correct spelling and word limits.
levels.extension: Name the distractor the speaker mentions for Questions 6 and 9.
levels.high_band: Explain the whole process aloud in one minute from the flow chart alone.

blocks.title: Which TWO?
blocks.mode: Teacher-led mini-model; read aloud live from the slide

stimulus.title: Mini-model (teacher reads aloud)
paragraphs: Visitors don't need to book in advance, although many people do. Please wear comfortable shoes, because the tour involves a lot of walking. Cameras are welcome, and you can take photos anywhere except in the laboratory. Finally, please switch off your phone before we go into the lecture hall.

items.prompt: Which TWO things must visitors do? A book in advance / B wear comfortable shoes / C leave cameras outside / D switch off their phones / E avoid the laboratory
items.reason: Booking is optional ('don't need to'), cameras are allowed, and the laboratory is only closed to photos. D: 'please switch off your phone'.

blocks.title: Predict the flow chart
blocks.instructions: Look at the flow chart for the bakery recording. What kind of answer does each gap need? Write N for a noun, V for a verb (past participle) or No for a number.

items.prompt: Flour is kept in sealed bins to protect it from ______.
items.evidence: 'From' is followed by a noun: something that damages flour.
items.reason: A preposition before the gap means a noun.

items.prompt: The dough rests for about ______ hours.
items.reason: Plural hours tells you the number is more than one.

items.prompt: Each loaf is ______ so they are all the same size.
items.evidence: 'Is ...' in a process needs a past participle (passive).

blocks.support: Foundation: the teacher reads each box aloud and asks 'a thing, an action or a number?'

blocks.title: A community bakery
blocks.mode: Guided listening practice: one play under practice conditions, then teacher-controlled review
blocks.instructions: Questions 1-2 and 3-4: choose TWO letters, A-E. Questions 5-10: complete the flow chart. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

stimulus.title: Recording IELTS-X4-L1 transcript (teacher-private)
paragraphs: VOLUNTEER: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Riverside Community Bakery. My name's Sam, and I'm one of the volunteers here. Before you start your first shift, I'll explain what we do and how the bread is made.

VOLUNTEER: We're a small bakery, but we produce around four hundred loaves a week. About half are sold to local cafés, and the profits pay for the rest, which go free of charge to the food bank and two shelters for homeless people. People often think we're funded by the council, but in fact we don't receive any grants at all. Everything comes from sales and from donations of flour from a local mill.

VOLUNTEER: Now, a couple of things about working here. Volunteers don't need any experience: we'll train you on the job. What we do ask is that you come for at least one shift a week, because it takes time to learn the routine. And for hygiene reasons, you must tie back long hair and remove any rings and watches before you start. You don't need to bring an apron; we provide those, and they're washed here.

VOLUNTEER: Right, the process. Everything starts in the store room, where the flour is kept in sealed bins to protect it from damp. Each morning we weigh out the flour and take it to the mixing table. There, it's combined with water, salt and yeast. We used to mix everything by hand, but now we use a large electric mixer, which saves a lot of time.

VOLUNTEER: After mixing, the dough needs to rest so that the yeast can do its work. We cover the bowls and leave them in the warmest room in the building, which is next to the oven, for about two hours. This stage is called proving. You'll know the dough is ready when it has doubled in size.

VOLUNTEER: Then comes shaping. This is still done by hand, because the machines we tried tore the dough. Each loaf is weighed so that they're all the same size, and then shaped and placed in a tin. The tins go into our wood-fired oven, which we heat to about two hundred and fifty degrees. The loaves take around forty minutes to bake.

VOLUNTEER: When they come out, the loaves have to cool completely before they can be wrapped, otherwise they become soft and damp. So we put them on metal racks by the back door, where there's a good flow of air. Finally, the bread is delivered. We used to use a van, but now most deliveries are made by bicycle, using cargo bikes that can carry up to forty loaves each.
VOLUNTEER: OK, any questions before we go into the kitchen?

items.prompt: Questions 1-2. Which TWO statements about the bakery are correct?
items.evidence: About half are sold to local cafés
items.reason: B: half the loaves are sold to cafés. C: 'donations of flour from a local mill'. A is the trap: 'we don't receive any grants at all'. D and E are not mentioned.
options: A  It receives money from the council.
B  Half of its bread is sold to cafés.
C  It is given flour by a mill.
D  It sells bread at a weekly market.
E  It was started by a homeless charity.

items.prompt: Questions 3-4. Which TWO things must volunteers do?
items.evidence: you come for at least one shift a week
items.reason: B: 'at least one shift a week'. D: 'remove any rings and watches'. Experience and aprons are explicitly not needed; no course is mentioned.
options: B  work at least one shift a week

items.prompt: Store room: flour kept in sealed bins to protect it from ______
items.reason: The first stage of the process.

items.prompt: Mixing: flour, water, salt and yeast combined in an electric ______
items.evidence: now we use a large electric mixer
items.reason: 'By hand' was the old method: a distractor.

items.prompt: Proving: dough rests for about ______ hours
items.reason: Write the number; 'two' is also accepted.

items.prompt: Shaping: each loaf is ______ so they are the same size
items.evidence: Each loaf is weighed so that they're all the same size

items.prompt: Baking: about ______ minutes in a wood-fired oven
items.evidence: The loaves take around forty minutes to bake
items.reason: Two hundred and fifty is the temperature, not the time.

items.prompt: Cooling: loaves placed on metal ______ by the back door
items.evidence: we put them on metal racks by the back door

blocks.flow_note: Questions 5-10 are a flow chart: store room -> mixing -> proving -> shaping -> baking -> cooling.
blocks.marking: For each 'choose TWO' pair, give one mark for each correct letter, in either order.
blocks.support: Foundation: a teacher-controlled second play with pauses after each stage of the process is allowed after the first attempt and recorded as support.
blocks.extension: For Questions 6 and 9, write the distractor the speaker mentions.
blocks.high_band: From your flow chart only, explain the whole process aloud in one minute.

stages.title: Opening challenge: which TWO?
stages.student: Listen to a short talk read aloud once and choose two letters.
stages.teacher: Read the mini-model once at natural speed. Reveal and show the three traps: optional, allowed, partly restricted.
stages.say: In 'choose TWO' questions, three options are usually mentioned but rejected or changed.
stages.check: Learners can say why A is wrong.

stages.title: Choose TWO: strategy
stages.student: Note the steps: underline the key idea in each option; listen for words like 'don't need', 'except', 'used to'; tick and cross as you listen.
stages.teacher: Teach that the five options are usually heard in order but the two answers can come anywhere. Learners mark each option as they hear it.
stages.say: Cross out options as they are rejected; do not wait until the end.
stages.check: Learners can list three words that signal a rejected option.

stages.title: Predict the flow chart
stages.student: Predict the type of answer for three boxes, then check.
stages.teacher: Reveal after learners commit. Point out that flow charts follow the order of the talk.
stages.say: Know what you are listening for before the recording starts.
stages.check: Learners can name the answer type for each box.

stages.title: Prepare for the recording
stages.student: Read Questions 1-10. Underline key ideas in the options and predict the flow-chart answers.
stages.teacher: The recording gives 30 seconds; allow up to 2 more minutes for preparation.
stages.say: ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for the flow chart.
stages.check: Each learner has predictions beside the boxes.

stages.title: The recording: one play
stages.teacher: Play IELTS-X4-L1 once without pausing. If audio fails, stop and use another listening activity; never read the transcript as a substitute.
stages.say: Follow the process from box to box.
stages.check: All answers committed before the review.

stages.title: Review: answers and distractors
stages.student: Check answers. Mark listening, spelling and word-limit errors separately.
stages.teacher: Reveal in pairs. Ask what was rejected for Q1-2 (council grants) and Q6 (mixing by hand). Optional teacher-controlled second play with pauses, recorded as support.
stages.say: Used to, but now: the answer is what happens now.
stages.check: Learners can explain the Q6 distractor.

stages.title: Explain the process
stages.student: In pairs, explain how the bread is made using your flow chart and sequence words. Then swap.
stages.teacher: Model the first two stages. Listen for sequence words and passive forms.
stages.say: Your flow chart should let you rebuild the whole process.
stages.check: Each learner explains the process once.

stages.title: My listening log
stages.student: Record each wrong answer as a listening, spelling or word-limit error, and set one target.
stages.teacher: Note the error types learners actually record. No band conversion.
stages.say: Choose TWO questions reward patience: wait for the final decision.

stages.title: Exit ticket and homework
stages.student: Complete the exit ticket and take the homework.
stages.teacher: Collect exit tickets. Assign online practice only through the existing workflow. Record the fresh-check date.
stages.say: Next time, cross out options as you hear them rejected.

Write five sentences describing the process using the passive (is mixed, is baked).

stimulus.title: Recording IELTS-X4-C1 transcript (teacher-private)
paragraphs: GUIDE: Thanks for coming to the Hillside Orchard open day. I'm going to tell you a little about the orchard and then explain how we turn our apples into juice.

GUIDE: The orchard is looked after entirely by volunteers, and we don't use any chemical sprays. The juice is sold at the village shop, and the money pays for new trees. Visitors sometimes ask whether they can pick apples themselves. I'm afraid that isn't possible, for insurance reasons, but you're welcome to walk around.

GUIDE: The apples are picked in September and October and stored in a cool barn. First, they're washed in large tanks of cold water, and any damaged fruit is removed by hand. The clean apples are then crushed in a mill, which turns them into a rough pulp. The pulp is wrapped in cloths and placed in a press, which squeezes out the juice.
GUIDE: Before bottling, the juice is heated to seventy-five degrees to kill any bacteria, and then it's poured into glass bottles. Unopened, the bottles keep for about a year.

items.prompt: Questions 1-2. Which TWO statements about the orchard are correct?
items.evidence: The orchard is looked after entirely by volunteers
items.reason: A: 'entirely by volunteers'. C: sold at the village shop. B is negated; D is refused; E: the money pays for trees.
options: A  Volunteers do all the work.
B  Chemical sprays are used occasionally.
C  The juice is sold in the village shop.
E  The money pays for a new building.

items.prompt: Apples washed in tanks of cold ______
items.evidence: washed in large tanks of cold water
The pulp is wrapped in cloths

items.prompt: Juice heated to ______ degrees before bottling
items.evidence: the juice is heated to seventy-five degrees
